ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer with the chat transcript and the GPS/timeline record: the SAFE-1 threat in F11 requires human handling, and the reviewer should decide the $6.61 no-show fee together with that conduct; NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are met on the trace, so the fee stands unless the reviewer waives it as a conduct sanction. No account flag is raised on this record.
ruling.reasoning:
Rider-filed no-show dispute over a $6.61 cancellation fee [F4][F7], cancelled_by = driver, so the fee is tested against NS-0 and NS-1 [NS-0][NS-1]. The NS-1 elements are settled by system records, not by statements: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 while 38 m from the pickup [F6], within the 200 m arrival radius, and stayed continuously inside the radius for 3 min 40 s after the tap, past the 3:01 default, until cancellation at 09:54:25 [F6][F3][F5][F4]. The platform's separate auto-arrival record at 09:49:50 [F5] is an earlier, distinct event and does not contradict the tap; on cumulative presence the driver was within 200 m for 4 min 35 s [F2]. On these records NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) are met and the fee would be earned, which is why the trace's allowed outcomes are no_action or escalate [NS-1]. The driver's post-hoc statement that he waited and cancelled as a no-show [F13] adds nothing beyond the records, and is not needed [NS-1].

The mandatory safety screen is what decides this case. Chat #3 sent at 09:54, a minute before the cancellation, reads "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it" [F11]. Read in context this is not a pickup arrangement or route rudeness: it is a threat aimed at the rider who is late, satisfying SAFE-1 (threats and intimidation), and the rider's complaint repeats the same allegation [F11][F4]. Every message is timestamped so the sequence is unambiguous [F12]. A threat under SAFE-1 bars an automatic ruling and sends the case to a person, so ruling = escalate [SAFE-1]. I record no dangerous-driving, accident or injury allegation, so SAFE-2 is not engaged [F11].

That leaves the fee for the human. The money at stake is the $6.61 cancellation fee on record [F4][F7]; there is no surge, so the charge carries no inflated component of its own [F8][FARE-1]. Under NS-7 any refund would issue as a voucher, and Ryde retains final discretion — so the recommended handling is to place the fee and the threat before the reviewer together, since the rider's objection is to the driver's conduct in the same chat, and the rider's "2 min, coming" at 09:52 shows she was still engaging with the booking [F10][NS-7].

No account flag is raised by this ruling. The NS-2 abuse-flag condition — tapping "I'm Here" while GPS shows the driver away from the pickup — is not met, because the tap occurred 38 m from the pickup [F6], and the driver's upheld history in the last 90 days is a no-show, not a route dispute, so RD-6's premise is absent [F18]. The profile facts are recorded but decide nothing on their own [F17][F18].

Evidence status is sufficient: the wait is covered by GPS without a hole from arrival to cancellation and every chat message is timestamped [F2][F6][F12]; nothing my ruling needs is missing. I make no segment findings — this is a no-show case with no off-route segment in the record.

NS-1's (iii) requires a continuous in-radius wait after the arrival confirmation, and the record provides it [F6][F1][F2][F3][NS-1]. This is a settled element, not one open to an undetermined finding.

There is no documentary inconsistency: F6 is the driver's own I'm Here tap at 09:50:45, 38 m from the pickup, and F5's 09:49:50 platform arrival record is a distinct earlier event. NS-1(i)(ii) are satisfied by the driver tap inside the radius [F5][F6][F1][NS-1]. The driver's statement F13 is unnecessary to the finding and is not relied on.

NS-2 returns the $6.61 only where NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) fail; on this record all three are met [F6][F2][F3][F5][NS-1][NS-2], so no refund is computed. Any refund here rests on NS-7 / the human reviewer's conduct decision, not on a fee element that failed.

RD-4 is not engaged: the driver did not cancel for traffic reasons and no traffic excuse is claimed, and F14/F15 show no speed-band or incident records [F14][F15][RD-4]. A no-show cancellation is tested under NS-1, not NS-3 [NS-1][NS-3].

No flag_account is available on this record: the NS-2 abuse-flag condition requires the I'm Here tap to be made while GPS shows the driver away from the pickup, but F6 places the tap 38 m from it, and RD-6 is premised on an upheld route-deviation finding, while F18 records only a no-show dispute [F6][F18][NS-2][RD-6]. The threat in F11 is dealt with at the human stage under SAFE-1.

Not disputed as to the rider's own conduct, but it does not create a refund: the rider's timely updates and clean profile [F10][F17] do not alter NS-1, whose elements are met on the system records [F6][F2][F5][NS-1]. Profile facts never decide a case on their own [F17].

Accepted as to effect: F11 is a threat and SAFE-1 applies, which is why the ruling is escalate; no fee consequence follows automatically from the threat itself, that is for the human under NS-7 [F11][SAFE-1][NS-7].
SAFE-2 is not engaged; the rider's own brief does not assert an accident, injury or dangerous-driving claim, and no such record exists [F11][SAFE-2]. The escalation rests on SAFE-1 alone.

Accepted to the extent that no FARE-1 overcharge component exists (the $6.61 with no surge is the published cancellation fee) [F7][F8][FARE-1], but the fee's final treatment cannot be settled automatically once SAFE-1 is engaged [SAFE-1].

Correct as to NS-1(i)(ii) [F1][F5][F6][NS-1], but passing those elements does not end the case once the SAFE-1 threat in F11 is on the record [F11][SAFE-1].
Accepted: no NS-2 abuse flag (tap made 38 m from pickup, F6) and RD-6 is not engaged (F18 shows a no-show, not a route dispute) [F6][F18][NS-2][RD-6]. The threat in F11 remains for the human stage.
Accepted as to the mechanics (driver tap at 09:50:45, 38 m; platform arrival 09:49:50) [F5][F6][NS-1], but it does not dispose of the SAFE-1 escalation [F11][SAFE-1].
Correct on NS-1(iii) [F2][F3][F5][F6][NS-1], but it does not produce no_action because the SAFE-1 screen takes the case to a human [F11][SAFE-1].
Accepted as corroboration of the wait [F10][F13][NS-1]; F13 itself remains a statement that carries no independent weight, and neither fact resolves the SAFE-1 issue [F11][SAFE-1].
Accepted: F11 is a threat and the driver does not contest that reading; SAFE-1 governs [F11][SAFE-1].
